title: feat(outage-park): park and reroute work blocked only by an unavailable service
body:
## Background

Every current route for an unavailable external service ends the same
way: post a hold comment and stop. That leaves the claim live until
`claimTiming.staleAge` elapses, so the session can neither continue nor
pick up different work, and the issue does not advertise why it is
stuck. Meanwhile the outage keeps producing more pull requests in the
same state, and each one adds branch-sync churn and a review backlog
that all lands at once on recovery.

Parking is the only relief route that costs no assurance at all: the
quality gates are untouched, and only scheduling changes. That makes it
the right default layer, and the only one available at all when both
services are degraded at once.

Blocked by #2319

## Proposed change

Add an explicit park-and-reroute route for work whose sole blocker is
an unavailable service, expressed in the existing hold/suspend
vocabulary rather than as a new lifecycle state.

- Enter the route only when the service verdict is `unavailable` and
  the pull request's blocker set contains nothing but that service.
  Any other blocker keeps today's behavior.
- On entry, post a park notice naming the service and the blocking
  evidence, then release the claim explicitly instead of waiting out
  the stale-age window, so the issue becomes reclaimable immediately
  and the session is free to route elsewhere.
- Bound the parked backlog with `providerOutage.maxParkedChanges`
  (documented small default). Once the bound is reached, the session
  stops claiming new issues rather than manufacturing more unmergeable
  pull requests.
- Add a read-only helper that lists parked pull requests and, for each,
  whether its blocking service has returned to `healthy`, in a
  deterministic order a later session can re-enter from.
- Change nothing about review, merge, or thread state: parking never
  resolves a thread, never marks a gate satisfied, and never merges.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The park route is documented in the phase instructions with its
      exact precondition (verdict `unavailable`, and no blocker other
      than that service) and its explicit claim release.
- [ ] A JSON Schema and read-only helper list parked and resumable
      pull requests from markers, with the contract registered in
      `docs/idd-helper-scripts.md`.
- [ ] Unit tests from offline fixtures assert no park happens on a
      `healthy`, `degraded`, or `unknown` verdict, and none happens
      when any additional blocker is present.
- [ ] Unit tests assert the parked-change bound is enforced at and just
      above the limit, and that reaching it stops new claims.
- [ ] A test asserts the park path performs no thread resolution, no
      gate satisfaction, and no merge, and that merge-readiness output
      for a parked pull request still reports its blockers.
- [ ] Resume ordering is deterministic for a fixed fixture set and is
      asserted by a test.
- [ ] `providerOutage.maxParkedChanges` validates against the schema,
      absence resolves to the documented default, and an invalid value
      is rejected deterministically.
- [ ] Behavior detail lands in `docs/`, the phase-instruction delta
      stays minimal, and `node scripts/audit-docs.mjs --check` passes
      the documentation byte budget.
- [ ] `pnpm run build` regenerates committed helper output, and
      `node scripts/validate-schemas.mjs` plus the repository's
      `pre-push-validate` command pass.

## Candidate files

- `src/scripts/provider-outage-park.mts`
- `schemas/provider-outage-park.schema.json`
- `src/scripts/policy-helpers.mts`
- `schemas/policy.schema.json`
- `.github/instructions/idd-overview-appendix.instructions.md`
- `idd-template/.github/instructions/idd-overview-appendix.instructions.md`
- `.github/instructions/idd-ci.instructions.md`
- `idd-template/.github/instructions/idd-ci.instructions.md`
